title: Higgsfield AI Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits and Costs
summary: Higgsfield AI pricing ranges from $99 to $375 monthly. Compare the cost per 1,000 credits across plans to find which tier offers the best value.
body_markdown:
## Testing before choosing your Higgsfield plan


Run the free tier on your real prompt, log the credits each finished clip costs for a week, and buy the plan whose credit allowance covers that figure. Credits per finished clip, not the monthly price, is what you actually pay.


### Measure credits per finished clip


The cost per kept clip from the last comparison only works if the credit side of the formula is your own measurement, not a vendor's example.


1.


Run the free tier on the prompt you'll use in production, not a test prompt. Use the same length, the same reference images, and the same model setting.


2.


Log the credits spent on every finished clip for one working week. Count a clip as finished only when you would publish it. Rejected takes still belong in the log, because their credits are spent, so attach them to the clip they eventually produced.


3.


Divide. Total credits spent that week, divided by finished clips, gives credits per clip. Multiply by the clips you expect to make in a month and you have the monthly allowance you need.


4.


Pick the plan whose monthly credit allowance covers that figure with some room. Read the allowance and the price from Higgsfield's own pricing page, not from a review or a screenshot. If you land just above a plan's allowance, price the top-up against the next plan up before choosing.


5.


Set a calendar reminder to re-check the pricing page. Credit allowances and what each generation costs in credits can change without your usage changing at all, so the plan that fit this month may not fit next quarter.


Four columns in a plain spreadsheet are enough: date, prompt label, credits spent, and whether the clip shipped. That's the whole instrument.


### Choosing a plan from the number


The purchase itself follows from the number. If credits per clip is high, the cheapest plan is false economy, since you'll run out mid-month and pay for top-ups.


If it's low, the larger plan is wasted money, and the pricing page is where you confirm which side of that line you are on.
